newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Jan-Oct retail sales fall 1.2 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Jan-Oct retail sales fall 1.2 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Bulgarian retail sales in the first 10 months of 1996 fell a real 1.2 percent from a year earlier due to a drop in the lev against the dollar and soaring inflation, the National Statistics Institute (NSI) said.
BULGARIA RETAIL SALES JAN-OCT JAN-SEPT JAN-OCT'95

"The constant depreciation of the lev against the dollar and high inflation have eroded consumers' purchasing power, which resulted in a decline of retail sales," an NSI official told a news conference.
The lev fell to 244-245 per dollar at the end of October from around 70 at the beginning of the year. Cumulative consumer price inflation for the first 10 months was 195.1 percent.
In October,retailers sold goods and services worth a total 103.3 billion levs, down a real 19.4 percent from the same month last year, the NSI said.
Sales of foods in October were a real 24.6-percent lower than in October 1995, and non-food sales declined by a real 14.3 percent, NSI figures showed. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
